base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a neighborhood block party by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

hidden_state.value: You are a friendly neighbor organizing a Saturday block party potluck for your cul-de-sac. You will introduce the attending households and their backgrounds across several turns. Some people will drop out, one person's health restriction gets lifted, and a new family joins late. At the end you will list specific dishes people plan to bring and ask if there are any problems. You must NEVER hint at what the specific problems are — just list the dishes and ask openly.

You are a calm, friendly neighborhood organizer. You always refer to your neighbors by name in third person (e.g. 'Mrs. Nguyen told me...', 'Mr. Henderson said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal party coordination — people dropping in and out is just how block parties work.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for neighbor updates

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have clear problems. Pulled pork sliders: Mrs. Nguyen is Jain (no meat). Peanut satay chicken skewers: Mateo has a severe peanut allergy (peanut satay) AND Mrs. Nguyen is Jain (chicken is meat). Garden salad with root vegetables and ranch dressing: Mrs. Nguyen is Jain (root vegetables like carrots, potatoes, onions are forbidden in Jain diet). Fruit platter is fine for everyone. Brownies made with almond flour are fine — almond flour is gluten-free, so they work for Lily (celiac), and Mr. Henderson's sugar restriction has been lifted by his doctor. The agent should NOT flag high sugar for Mr. Henderson (his doctor cleared him). The agent should NOT remove Mateo's peanut allergy just because his parents left — Mateo is still at the party.
required_elements: Pulled pork sliders are problematic: Mrs. Nguyen grew up Jain, cannot eat meat
Peanut satay chicken skewers are problematic for Mateo: he had a severe peanut allergy reaction (throat swelled, EpiPen used), peanut satay contains peanuts
Peanut satay chicken skewers are also problematic for Mrs. Nguyen: chicken is meat, Jain diet forbids meat
Garden salad with root vegetables is problematic for Mrs. Nguyen: Jain diet forbids root vegetables
Fruit platter is fine for everyone currently attending
Brownies made with almond flour are fine — almond flour is gluten-free, safe for Lily who is celiac
Mr. Henderson has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent does not flag sugar content for him
forbidden_elements: Flagging brownies or sweet items as problematic for Mr. Henderson (his doctor cleared him, restriction removed)
Removing Mateo's peanut allergy because his parents left the party (Mateo himself is still there)

Saying Mateo has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy — almond flour brownies are fine for him unless agent has reason to flag cross-reactivity, but the scenario specifies peanut only)
Ignoring Mrs. Nguyen's Jain dietary constraints entirely
Ignoring the root vegetable restriction for Mrs. Nguyen (Jain diet specifically forbids root vegetables, not just meat)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across a block party planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Mrs. Nguyen grew up Jain → Jain dietary laws → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (inferential chain, never explicitly stated as dietary rules), (2) Mateo has a severe peanut allergy (direct from EpiPen incident), (3) Mr. Henderson's diabetes/low-sugar restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared him), (4) Garcia parents EXIT but Mateo STAYS — his peanut allergy remains active for all shared food (scope distinction: child stays after parents leave), (5) The Chen family JOINS late with Lily who is celiac (late-joining high-constraint entity). At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state: Mrs. Nguyen = Jain (no meat, no root vegetables), Mateo = peanut allergy (still present at party), Lily = celiac (no gluten). Mr. Henderson's sugar restriction no longer applies. Key traps: brownies with almond flour LOOK problematic for celiac Lily but almond flour is gluten-free (trap — looks bad but isn't); garden salad with root vegetables requires knowing Jain diet forbids root vegetables (not just meat); Mr. Henderson being flagged for sugar despite being cleared (removed constraint ghost); Mateo's peanut allergy disappearing because his parents left (scope error — child stays).

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
